# Resource: yet_cloud_pool

Runtimes that run the same environments together — across servers, or clouds.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Two runtimes, on two clouds, running the same environments — behind one tunnel.
resource "yet_cloud_pool" "web" {
  name        = "web"
  color       = "violet"
  runtime_ids = [yet_cloud_runtime.office.id, yet_cloud_runtime.aws.id]
  tunnel      = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Its name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 32, starting with a letter.

### Optional

- `color` (String) How Cloud draws it: `gray`, `red`, `orange`, `amber`, `green`, `teal`, `sky`, `blue`, `violet`, `pink`.
- `description` (String) What it is for.
- `move_environments` (Boolean) Whether the environments of runtimes joining move onto the pool, or stay theirs. Cloud asks when a joining runtime has some.
- `runtime_ids` (Set of String) Its members.
- `tunnel` (Boolean) Whether it is behind a Cloudflare tunnel of its own — its edge, for every member — or its members are each reached on their own. Opening or closing it is a Cloud admin's.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `tunnel_id` (String) Its Cloudflare tunnel, when it has one.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, with an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import):

```terraform
import {
  to = yet_cloud_pool.web
  id = "01J9Z8K3V7Q2M4N6P8R0S2T4V6"
}
```

With [`terraform import`](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import):

```shell
terraform import yet_cloud_pool.web 01J9Z8K3V7Q2M4N6P8R0S2T4V6
```
